r1.title: The problem
r1.sub: rank fraud well, then pick the cheapest threshold
r1.body:
A card issuer scores every transaction. Scores above a threshold go to step-up (manual review or extra authentication such as OTP / 3-D Secure); the rest are approved. Two mistakes cost money in different ways: a good customer stepped up (friction and review effort) and a missed fraud (the amount is lost).

So the goal has two parts: a model that ranks fraud well, measured by PR-AUC because only {{fraud_rate}} of transactions are fraud, and a threshold that minimises total expected cost rather than one that maximises an accuracy-style metric.
r2.title: Data and its limits
r2.body:
• Credit Card Fraud Detection 2026 by Udit Jain on Kaggle, released under CC0. It is a public dataset of unspecified provenance: the data card does not say whether rows are real or synthetic, so no result here is a claim about real-world card fraud.
  • {{n_rows}} transactions, {{n_fraud}} of them fraud ({{fraud_rate}}, {{ci_level}} CI {{fraud_rate_ci}}), {{n_features}} features. {{n_checks_failed}} of {{n_checks}} structural data checks failed.
  • Hints of synthetic generation: channel and device look statistically independent (p = {{chan_dev_p}}), and the smallest fraud is {{fraud_min_usd}}.
  • No customer or card ID and no real timestamp, so no customer-history features, no grouped split and no out-of-time test.
  • The split was locked before any label-based analysis: a development set of {{dev_n}} rows ({{dev_fraud}} fraud) for {{n_folds_k}}-fold cross-validation repeated {{n_repeats}} times, and a holdout of {{holdout_n}} rows ({{holdout_fraud}} fraud) scored once at the end.
  • The live stream above is a random sample of {{stream_n}} dev rows ({{stream_fraud}} fraud); it contains no holdout rows.
r3.title: Main results
r3.body:
Final model: {{final_model}}. A random score has PR-AUC ≈ {{noskill}} (the fraud rate); the model reaches about {{cv_lift}}× that on cross-validation.

Cross-validation on the dev split vs the holdout, scored once. Brackets are {{ci_level}} confidence intervals (CV: across {{n_cv_folds}} folds; holdout: stratified bootstrap).
metricCV on devholdout ({{ho_fraud}} fraud)
PR-AUC (primary){{cv_pr_auc}} {{cv_pr_auc_ci}}{{ho_pr_auc}} {{ho_pr_auc_ci}}
ROC-AUC{{cv_roc_auc}} {{cv_roc_auc_ci}}{{ho_roc_auc}} {{ho_roc_auc_ci}}
Recall at threshold {{threshold}}{{cv_recall}}{{ho_recall}} {{ho_recall_ci}}
Precision at that threshold{{cv_precision}}{{ho_precision}} {{ho_precision_ci}}
Share stepped up{{cv_alert_rate}}{{ho_alert_rate}} {{ho_alert_rate_ci}}

The holdout agrees with CV within its (wide) intervals. Logistic regression beat the best gradient boosting pipeline ({{best_boost_name}}, PR-AUC {{best_boost_pr_auc}}): boosting minus logistic = {{boost_vs_lr_diff}} {{boost_vs_lr_ci}}. On this dataset the fraud odds multiply with each extra red flag ({{flag_odds_multipliers}} per flag), the additive log-odds shape a logistic model represents directly. That is a statement about this data, not about fraud models in general.

The step-up threshold {{threshold}} was chosen on dev out-of-fold predictions only (per-repeat optimum {{thr_repeat_range}}). On CV it catches {{cv_recall}} of fraud while stepping up {{cv_alert_rate}} of transactions, about {{alerts_per_fraud}} step-ups per fraud found.
r4.title: What drives the score
r4.sub: top three features carry {{shap_top3_share}} of mean |SHAP|
r4.body:
Mean absolute SHAP value per feature on the dev split (log-odds units; exact linear SHAP for the logistic model, one-hot columns summed back to their source feature). The top three — {{shap_top3}} — carry {{shap_top3_share}} of the total.

{{shap_html}}

A false alarm and a caught fraud can carry the same red flags. Separating them more likely needs information this dataset does not have (customer history) than a different algorithm.
r5.title: What didn’t work
r5.sub: SMOTE {{smote_diff}} · decline tier not distinguishable on holdout
r5.body:
Every comparison was pre-registered: the simpler option is kept unless the {{ci_level}} CI of the paired difference (corrected resampled t-test over {{n_cv_folds}} folds) excludes zero.

{{forest_html}}
  • SMOTE hurt badly ({{smote_diff}} {{smote_ci}}). SMOTENC fills categorical and boolean features by neighbour majority vote, so synthetic fraud carried red flags only {{smote_flag_ratio}}× as often as real fraud (IP-country mismatch: {{smote_ipmis_real}} of real fraud vs {{smote_ipmis_syn}} of synthetic).
  • Class weights and undersampling were not distinguishable from doing nothing.
  • Calibration: {{calibration_verdict}}.
  • Splines and red-flag interactions (checked later, pre-registered) were not distinguishable from the plain logistic model: {{gam_diff}} {{gam_ci}} and {{pairs_diff}} {{pairs_ci}}.

A third tier (“decline”) did not clearly pay off

Approve / step-up / decline, with thresholds {{tt_stepup}} and {{tt_decline}} chosen on CV, looked cheaper on CV ({{tt_cv_diff}} per {{per_n}} transactions vs two tiers with the same model). On the holdout the difference was {{ho_tt_diff}} {{ho_tt_diff_ci}} per {{per_n}}: the interval includes zero, so the simpler two-tier policy is recommended. Assumes {{tt_pass_rate_pct}} of fraudsters pass step-up and a wrongly declined good customer costs {{tt_decline_fp}} USD. {{cost_label}}.
r6.title: Fairness by age
r6.sub: {{fair_n_real}} of {{fair_n_comparisons}} gaps pass the pre-registered rule · not a fairness claim
r6.body:
Step-up rate, recall, precision and false-positive rate per age band at the project threshold {{fair_threshold}}, on dev out-of-fold scores; the holdout was not used. The rule was written before the results: a gap between a band and everyone else counts only if its Bonferroni-adjusted interval ({{fair_n_comparisons}} comparisons) excludes zero.

{{fairness_html}}
  • {{fair_headline}} ({{fair_n_real}} of {{fair_n_comparisons}}); the others are not distinguishable. That is not evidence of fairness — bands hold only {{fair_fraud_min}}–{{fair_fraud_max}} fraud cases and the widest adjusted interval spans {{fair_widest}}.
  • At the unadjusted {{ci_level}} level {{fair_n_95}} gaps exclude zero ({{fair_hint}}); {{fair_direction}}. A lead to re-check with more data, not a finding.
  • Without customer_age PR-AUC changes by {{noage_diff}} {{noage_ci}} ({{noage_verdict}}); step-up rate {{band_young}} {{noage_young}}, {{band_old}} {{noage_old}}. Age ranks {{age_shap_rank}} features by mean |SHAP|.
  • Age is the only person attribute in this data; no causal or legal claim is made.
r7.title: How the evaluation stays honest
r7.body:
• Holdout locked before any label-based analysis and scored once; a lock file refuses any other pipeline or threshold.
  • All preprocessing and resampling are fitted inside training folds; leakage guards run in the test suite.
  • Comparisons, metrics and decision rules were written down before the results (pre-registration with dated amendments).
  • The in-browser model is the Python pipeline exported as coefficients, one-hot categories and scaler parameters; a test checks that the browser’s score for every transaction on this page matches Python to within {{js_tol}}.
  • Every number on this page is generated from the project’s committed result files; nothing is typed by hand.
